title: Monitoring Deep‐Sea Shark Fisheries Under a Precautionary Framework and the Role of eDNA
content:
ABSTRACT

The reopening of the Maldivian gulper shark (Centrophorus spp.) fishery highlights the need for precautionary management under substantial uncertainty. Gulper sharks are among the least productive and most vulnerable marine species, with extremely slow recovery following overexploitation. Although reopening without evidence of recovery poses clear conservation risks, the precautionary principle is insufficiently operationalised in a proposal to use Environmental DNA (eDNA) to inform management, lacking defined reference points, recovery thresholds, or harvest control rules. eDNA, as currently applied, cannot meet the evidentiary requirements of precautionary fisheries management, as it provides presence-only information and cannot reliably indicate abundance, population structure, or recovery. eDNA should therefore complement, not replace, robust baseline data, species-specific assessments and explicit decision rules.
